agentCan: Register the client (one unauthenticated POST), generate PKCE values, and run the whole flow
Implement the 90-day re-authorization cycle and expiry-warning handling

approval.trigger: None. The DCR guide describes no CircleCI review, approval, listing, or marketplace step at any point. Client registration is unauthenticated and immediate; the only consent gate is the end user clicking Allow. There are no user caps before approval because there is no approval. The only per-organization gate is user-driven: for SSO-enabled organizations, the user must explicitly authorize each org on the consent screen.

blockers.detail: 'The redirect_uri must be a loopback address (127.0.0.1, ::1, or localhost) with a port in the range 1025-65535 and no query parameters.' The documented flow is built for local tools; the docs describe no hosted (https) redirect option for this flow. A hosted SaaS redirect flow does not fit.
blockers.howToClear: Use this flow for CLI/desktop/local agents. For a hosted product, the documented fallback is asking users to create and paste a personal or project API token.
blockers.title: Loopback-only redirect URIs

blockers.detail: 'This flow does not issue refresh tokens.' The token lasts 90 days (expires_in 7776000), then every user must re-run authorization. CircleCI emails personal-token expiry warnings 30, 15, 7, and 1 day before expiry.
blockers.howToClear: Build re-authorization into your product's lifecycle (prompts ahead of the 90-day cliff); there is no renewal shortcut.
blockers.title: No refresh tokens: re-authorize every 90 days

Exact authorization-code lifetime ('short-lived' is all the docs say).
Rate limits or quotas on the registration endpoint or DCR-issued tokens.
Whether CircleCI runs any abuse review/blocking of DCR clients behind the scenes (no review documented).
Any partner/marketplace program for OAuth tools (nothing in the docs ties one to this flow).

alternatives: Manually created personal API tokens (always full user permissions; user creates and pastes by hand)
Project API tokens (Status / Read Only / Admin; also manual, and not supported on API v2)
flavor.recommended: A dynamically registered OAuth client (RFC 7591 DCR) using authorization code + PKCE (S256, mandatory), built for tools that run on the user's own machine
flavor.why: There is no portal and no client secret: your tool registers itself once via POST app.circleci.com/oauth/register and receives only a client_id (token_endpoint_auth_method 'none'). 'No pre-shared client secret or manual token creation in the CircleCI web app is needed', and 'because no client secret is issued, this value does not need to be treated as sensitive. PKCE protects the flow instead.' The flow's output is not a generic access token: it is a standard CircleCI personal API token (prefix ccipat_) minted on behalf of the user.

humanMust: Hold a CircleCI account and be a member of an organization (stated prerequisite)
Click Allow at consent, choose the access level, and separately authorize any SSO-enabled organizations
Re-run authorization roughly every 90 days per token
name: CircleCI
nuances: Coarse scopes: no granular API scopes, only the three access levels Read / Write / Admin, chosen by the USER at consent time, not requested by the app. The level is 'a ceiling on the token, not a grant of new permissions': a Viewer who selects Admin still gets a read-only token.

SSO org trap: leaving an SSO org unauthorized 'does not fail the flow. The token is still issued, but it cannot access that org's resources.' Access can later be granted or revoked from the OAuth Clients page in user settings without redoing the flow.

Re-registration multiplies clients: 'Register only once per tool. Re-registering creates a new, separate client.' state is required on the authorize call; omitting it returns 400, and plain PKCE challenges are rejected (S256 only). Optional RFC 9126 Pushed Authorization Requests (POST /oauth/par) are supported.
Tokens are visible to and revocable by the user from their Personal API Tokens page, and API tokens 'cannot be modified after they have been created': change means delete and recreate.
Manual personal tokens contrast: they 'grant full read and write permissions' with a user-set expiry 'no more than one year in the future'.
prerequisites: A CircleCI account; you must be a member of an organization
A local redirect listener on a loopback port (1025-65535)

steps.detail: POST app.circleci.com/oauth/register with JSON: client_name, redirect_uris, grant_types ['authorization_code'], response_types ['code']. 'No authentication is required, and no client secret is issued.' Returns 201 with the client_id. Register only once per tool.
steps.title: Register the client dynamically (once per tool)

steps.detail: code_verifier (43-128 chars), code_challenge = base64url(sha256(verifier)), plus a random state. S256 is mandatory: 'CircleCI requires the S256 challenge method; plain code challenges are not accepted.'
steps.title: Generate PKCE values; start a loopback listener

steps.detail: GET app.circleci.com/oauth/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri (loopback only, port 1025-65535, no query parameters), code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256, state (required; omitting it returns 400). The user logs in, chooses the access level (Read / Write / Admin), separately authorizes any SSO-enabled organizations, and clicks Allow.
steps.title: Send the user to authorize

steps.detail: POST app.circleci.com/oauth/token, form-encoded: grant_type=authorization_code, code (single-use, short-lived), client_id, redirect_uri, code_verifier. Response: access_token (a ccipat_ personal API token), token_type Bearer, expires_in 7776000 (90 days). No refresh token is issued.
steps.title: Exchange the code

steps.detail: Use the token as a Bearer token on API v3 or v2 calls (v2 also accepts the Circle-Token header). Plan re-authorization before the 90-day expiry; CircleCI emails warnings at 30, 15, 7, and 1 day.
steps.title: Call the API; plan the 90-day re-authorization

tagline: OAuth with no portal at all: your tool registers itself with one unauthenticated POST, PKCE replaces the client secret, and the prize is a 90-day personal API token. The catch is structural: redirect URIs are loopback-only and there are no refresh tokens, so this fits local tools, not hosted SaaS.

time.active: One registration POST + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
